title: Natural coordinates for finite free internal scalar extension
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be an essentially small site with the sheafification and closed symmetric monoidal tensor of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] for abelian sheaves. Let $\varphi:R\to B$ be a morphism of commutative ring objects, and use internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and scalar extension and restriction [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Suppose given an $R$-module isomorphism $\theta:R^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_\varphi B$, for an integer $n\geq0$, with inverse coordinates $q_i:B\to R$. Write $b_i$ for the image of $1$ under the $i$th basis map $R\to B$ (and its restriction on each test object). There is a natural isomorphism of $R$-module valued functors
$$\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\bigl(B\otimes_R-\bigr)\xrightarrow{\sim}(-)^n.$$
For an $R$-module sheaf $M$, it and its inverse are specified on local elementary tensors and tuples by
$$\Phi_M(s\otimes m)=(q_i(s)m)_i,\qquad \Psi_M((m_i)_i)=\sum_i b_i\otimes m_i.$$
These formulas specify sheaf morphisms through the tensor and coequalizer universal properties; no equality of tensor-sheaf sections with sectionwise tensor products is asserted.

proof.text: Put $e_i=\theta\iota_i:R\to B$ and $q_i=\pi_i\theta^{-1}:B\to R$. The two inverse identities for $\theta$ give $q_i e_j=\delta_{ij}\operatorname{id}_R$ and $\sum_i e_i q_i=\operatorname{id}_B$. Since these are module maps, on every test object $U$ they say $q_i(b_j)=\delta_{ij}$ and $s=\sum_i\varphi(q_i(s))b_i$ for $s\in B(U)$, with $e_i(r)=\varphi(r)b_i$. Here $b_i=e_i(1)$ is compatible with every restriction. Define $M^n(U)=M(U)^n$ with componentwise action; gluing tuples componentwise makes this a sheaf and an $R$-module. Its finite sums and coordinate maps are likewise componentwise.

source.place: Last sentence, first inference: the natural finite-power description of tensor with a finite free coefficient ring

proof.text: For every $i$ the rule $(s,m)\mapsto q_i(s)m$ is additive in both variables and commutes with restrictions. The tensor universal property and sheafification of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] therefore give a sheaf map $B\otimes M\to M$. It equalizes the defining arrows for relative tensor in [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], because $q_i(s\varphi(r))m=rq_i(s)m=q_i(s)(rm)$. Thus it factors uniquely through $B\otimes_R M$. This factor is $R$-linear: $q_i(\varphi(r)s)m=r(q_i(s)m)$, and equality as sheaf maps follows from the same universal properties. Collect these factors into $\Phi_M:\operatorname{Res}_\varphi(B\otimes_R M)\to M^n$. This constructs the stated formula without requiring tensor sections to be sectionwise tensors.

source.place: Last sentence, first inference: the natural finite-power description of tensor with a finite free coefficient ring

proof.text: The unit sheaf map $\mathbf1\to R$ followed by $e_i$ gives a sheaf map $\mathbf1\to B$. Tensor it with $M$ using the inverse left unitor and then the coequalizer map $B\otimes M\to B\otimes_R M$. The resulting map $t_i:M\to B\otimes_R M$ sends $m$ to $b_i\otimes m$. It is $R$-linear because $b_i\otimes rm=(b_i\varphi(r))\otimes m=\varphi(r)(b_i\otimes m)$ by the coequalizer relation and commutativity of $B$. Define $\Psi_M=\sum_i t_i\operatorname{pr}_i$. Finite sums preserve restrictions and $R$-linearity, so this is a module-sheaf morphism with the required tuple formula.

source.place: Last sentence, first inference: the natural finite-power description of tensor with a finite free coefficient ring

proof.text: For a tuple $(m_j)_j$ of local sections, the $i$th coordinate of $\Phi_M\Psi_M((m_j)_j)$ is $\sum_j q_i(b_j)m_j=\sum_j\delta_{ij}m_j=m_i$. Thus the composite is the identity as a sheaf map (equality holds at every object), and hence as a module map.

source.place: Last sentence, first inference: the natural finite-power description of tensor with a finite free coefficient ring

proof.text:
Precompose the other composite with the defining map $B\otimes M\to B\otimes_R M$. On an elementary tensor of local sections its value is
$$\Psi_M\Phi_M(s\otimes m)=\sum_i b_i\otimes(q_i(s)m)=\sum_i(b_i\varphi(q_i(s)))\otimes m=s\otimes m.$$
The middle equality is the balancing relation; the last uses $\sum_i e_iq_i=\operatorname{id}_B$. Equality on these tensors implies equality of the maps out of the objectwise abelian tensor presheaf by its bilinear universal property, hence equality out of its sheafification $B\otimes M$. Uniqueness in the coequalizer universal property then gives $\Psi_M\Phi_M=\operatorname{id}$. This is a comparison of morphisms via universal properties, with no assertion that all relative-tensor sheaf sections are elementary tensors or sums of such sections on the same object.

source.place: Last sentence, first inference: the natural finite-power description of tensor with a finite free coefficient ring

proof.text: For a module morphism $f:M\to N$, scalar extension acts on elementary tensors by $s\otimes m\mapsto s\otimes f(m)$: this is its induced coequalizer map. The $i$th coordinate on the two sides of naturality of $\Phi$ is respectively $q_i(s)f(m)$ and $f(q_i(s)m)$, which agree by $R$-linearity of $f$. The tensor, sheafification and coequalizer uniqueness arguments of step 5 give equality of sheaf maps. Naturality of $\Psi$ follows as well from $\sum_i b_i\otimes f(m_i)$ on both sides (or from the inverse identities). Consequently these mutually inverse transformations give the required natural isomorphism. The formulas also cover $n=0$: the basis identity is $\operatorname{id}_B=0$, $M^0$ is the zero module, and the same empty-sum calculation proves both inverse identities. No nonzero-ring, nonzero-module, or positive-rank assumption is used.

The statement, stmt_deps, source and blueprint fields are unchanged from the record Q43 created; only split-owned fields changed. There are no new nodes, no repair note for this item, it is not on the route-pivot dropped list, and it cites no SGA. Step 1 gets the Kronecker identity q_i e_j=δ and s=Σφ(q_i s)b_i from θ's two inverse identities and R-linearity of e_i, q_i under the Res action. Step 2 builds Φ through the presheaf tensor, sheafification and the coequalizer. Its balancing check is correct: q_i(sφ(r))m=q_i(s)(rm) uses that B and R are commutative and the action is associative. Testing on the triple tensor is valid because sheafification is strong monoidal. Step 3 builds t_i=b_i⊗–, which is R-linear by the coequalizer relation. In step 4 the composite ΦΨ is the identity because q_i(b_j)=δ_ij. In step 5, ΨΦ(s⊗m)=s⊗m on elementary tensors, and uniqueness out of the bilinear tensor, the sheafification and the coequalizer gives ΨΦ=id. Step 6 proves naturality from the linearity of f. Every step is truly elementary from the cited statements. I tested n=0 (B=0, both sides zero), n=1 with b_1 a unit other than 1, and ordinary modules on a point. No candidate duplicates it: monoidal-finite-free-transport, det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-finite-free, scalar-model-finite-flat-resolution and sbc pullback-free-coordinates are all different statements.
